results.title: N. Korea to hold int'l Pyongyang marathon in Oct. 2027: tour agency
results.content: North Korea plans to hold an international marathon in its capital of Pyongyang in October next year, a tour agency that is an official partner of the event said Sunday. Koryo Tours, a Beijing-based tour agency specializing in North Korea, said in a social media post that the 2027 Pyongyang International Marathon would take place in October, adding that the exact date would be announced once officially confirmed. If held as planned, the event would mark a shift from its traditional schedule in April to October. North Korea has held the international marathon in Pyongyang since 1981 to mark the April 15 birthday of late national founder, Kim Il-sung. The marathon was not held for five consecutive years from 2020 due to the COVID-19 pandemic before resuming in 2025. results.title: Coast Guard finds hull of missing fishing boat Haegwangho on seabed
results.content: The Coast Guard said Sunday it confirmed that an object found on the seabed off Korea's west coast was the hull of the missing fishing boat Haegwangho, as the search entered its fifth day. The Coast Guard had been working to identify the object it had earlier discovered lying on the seabed near where the Haegwangho went missing off the western coastal county of Taean last Wednesday. Coast Guard officials confirmed that what had appeared to be a sunken ship was the missing boat. The Haegwangho, a 7.93-ton boat carrying three Koreans and four Indonesians, was reported missing early last Wednesday. It had left a port in Taean two days earlier.

results.title: Sungkyunkwan University forum explores advances in next-generation solar cells
results.content: Sungkyunkwan University hosted the 14th Sungkyun International Solar Forum at its Seoul campus from Nov. 11-13, bringing together researchers to discuss advances in perovskite solar cells and optoelectronic devices. The forum came amid growing demand for carbon-free energy sources to address the climate crisis, as electricity demand continues to rise due to the expansion of artificial intelligence (AI) data centers and the increasing adoption of electric vehicles. Commercializing perovskite solar cells, which are seen as a next-generation power generation technology, and developing technologies for mass production have emerged as key challenges. Park Nam-gyu, a distinguished professor of chemical engineering at the university and director of the SKKU National Laboratory for Intelligent Energy Solution Technology, chaired the forum’s organizing committee. results.title: World skating chief seeking further expansion of Short Track World Tour
results.content: The global skating chief said Sunday he is seeking further expansion of a revamped international short track speed skating circuit, with his native Korea likely to host at least one event every season. Kim Jae-youl, president of the International Skating Union (ISU), revealed his plans to add another competition to the ISU Short Track World Tour for next season and make it an eight-leg circuit. Kim earlier oversaw the makeover of the international short track competition, as the World Tour replaced the World Cup starting in the 2024-2025 season. The inaugural World Tour season featured six events. For the 2025-2026 season, with the Milan-Cortina Winter Olympics scheduled in February 2026, there were just four World Tour stops. results.title: Landers retain free agent pitcher Moon Seung-won
results.content: The SSG Landers announced Sunday they have retained their own free agent pitcher Moon Seung-won on a multiyear contract. The Landers said Moon agreed to a two-year pact with an option for a third season. He will receive 750 million won ($557,000) in total salary and a signing bonus of 500 million won. He can make another 250 million won in incentives. The 36-year-old has only pitched for the Landers franchise since making his Korea Baseball Organization debut in 2012, when they were called the SK Wyverns under different ownership. He helped the club win Korean Series titles in 2018 and 2022. In 2026, the right-hander matched his career high with 62 appearances, going 2-2 with 17 holds and two saves and a 3.45 ERA over 62 2/3 innings — his best ERA in a healthy season since 2020. results.title: Ruling party outlines grounds to impeach chief justice
results.content: The ruling Democratic Party of Korea (DPK) laid out its grounds Sunday for impeaching Supreme Court Chief Justice Cho Hee-dae and said it would seek a National Assembly vote by the end of December, drawing criticism that the move could undermine judicial independence. At its first public briefing at the Assembly, the party’s impeachment task force pointed to the Supreme Court’s handling of President Lee Jae Myung’s election law case and Cho’s refusal to recommend a new candidate for a vacant Supreme Court seat. “We will do our utmost to finalize the impeachment motion as quickly as possible and bring it to a vote in the National Assembly before the end of December,” said Rep. Yang Bu-nam, who leads the task force. He did not give a date for filing the motion. results.title: Half of Korean workers fear workplace photos could be used in AI sex crimes
results.content: More than half of workers in Korea worry that photos of themselves posted on company intranets or messaging platforms could be used in artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted sex crimes, a survey showed Sunday. According to the survey commissioned by labor rights group Workplace Gapjil 119 and conducted by polling firm Global Research, 53.1 percent of 1,000 workers aged 19 or older said they were concerned that their workplace photos could be exploited for such crimes. The survey was conducted from Aug. 1–7. The concern was more widespread among women, with 58.2 percent expressing anxiety, compared with 49 percent among male respondents. The survey also pointed to a lack of safeguards at companies. Only 11.6 percent of respondents said their employers had rules in place to prevent and respond to AI-related sex crimes. results.title: Korean consortium wins Vietnam high-speed rail design contract
results.content: The Korea National Railway and two Korean engineering firms will take part in a project to develop a high-speed railway connecting northern and southern Vietnam, spanning 1,541 kilometers between Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City, according to Korea's Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport, Sunday. A consortium comprising Korean, French and Vietnamese companies has won a contract for a feasibility study and front-end engineering design (FEED) for the project. The contract was tendered by the Thang Long Project Management Unit under Vietnam's Ministry of Construction. The consortium includes state-run Korea National Railway and Korean engineering firms Yooshin and Sambo, along with France's Systra and Vietnam's Tedi, both of which specialize in railway design. results.title: [COVER STORY] 'AI spending binge puts Samsung, SK at risk of memory price collapse'
results.content: Samsung Electronics and SK hynix could face a sharp memory price decline if hyperscalers scale back the artificial intelligence (AI) spending that has driven the current chip boom, according to a renowned U.S. semiconductor analyst. Jim Handy, founder and general director at Objective Analysis, said in an interview with The Korea Times that the surge in memory prices — caused by a sharp increase in demand — is “temporary,” echoing concerns among some Korean analysts that the current memory cycle may be nearing its peak. “I do not think that AI demand is growing that quickly, so they are likely to slow their spending at some point, and that will cause memory prices to collapse,” Handy said. Although the timing of a downturn is difficult to predict, memory prices could eventually fall back to 2024 levels once demand weakens, he said. results.title: 2026 Shenzhen APEC and North Korea
results.content: The 2026 Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit just concluded in Shenzhen, China at a critical moment for the international order at both the global and regional levels. The limelight belonged to the first-ever trilateral summit meeting held between the leaders of the United States, China and Russia, which drew the most media coverage. The trilateral meeting was historic, but it ended in an anti-climactic way. Except for a very generic statement, there were few tangible outcomes. It was heavy on optics but shallow in substance. Two outstanding regional conflicts — Ukraine and Iran — were not included in the statement, nor the two key issues in East Asia of security on the Korean Peninsula and the Taiwan Strait. results.title: Korea holds landmark Kimchi Day vision declaration in New York
results.content: The Ministry of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs said Sunday that it held its first-ever Kimchi Global Vision Declaration ceremony in New York on Friday (local time) to mark the seventh annual Kimchi Day and promote kimchi in global markets. Kimchi Day was first designated on Nov. 22, 2020 to honor kimchi's cultural heritage, ingredients and health benefits. The event, held at the Korean Cultural Center New York, brought together about 100 participants, including New York State Assemblymember Ron Kim, Korean Consul General in New York Kim Sang-ho, chef Hooni Kim and local food industry representatives. results.title: Kookmin University teams up with QNX to introduce Korea's first embedded software curriculum
results.content: Kookmin University established the QNX Centre Korea on Nov. 4 in partnership with QNX, a global provider of embedded software and operating systems, to provide specialized education in the field. The university said the center will serve as a platform for industry-academia collaboration aimed at nurturing talent in embedded software. Through the partnership, Kookmin University becomes the first university in Korea to introduce a curriculum based on QNX technology. QNX, a division of BlackBerry Limited, provides operating systems and software development technologies for industries where safety and reliability are critical, including the automotive, medical device and industrial automation sectors. results.title: Ramyeon exports set to approach $2 bil. this year on global popularity
results.content: Exports of "ramyeon," or instant noodles, are set to approach $2 billion this year amid the expanding global popularity of Korean food and culture, industry data showed Sunday. Ramyeon shipments rose 26.3 percent to $1.59 billion in the January-October period, already surpassing last year's full-year total of $1.52 billion, according to data from the Korea Agro-Fisheries & Food Trade Corp. If the growth trend continues through the rest of the year, annual ramyeon exports are expected to approach $2 billion. Korea's ramyeon exports have steadily increased since 2014. China was the biggest buyer, importing $395.5 million worth in the 10-month period, up 23.9 percent from a year earlier. Exports to the United States rose 29.1 percent to $276.5 million over the cited period. Exports to Europe and Central and South America also posted strong growth. results.title: Sogang University, KIST join forces on research, talent development
results.content: Sogang University and the Korea Institute of Science and Technology (KIST) have signed a memorandum of understanding to expand joint research and foster specialized talent in semiconductors, clean hydrogen and space-related composite materials. The agreement was signed by Sogang President Sim Jong-hyeok and KIST President Oh Sang-rok at the Sogang’s Seoul campus on Nov. 11, the universities said. The partnership will combine KIST’s mission-oriented research capabilities with Sogang’s academic and educational strengths to advance strategic technologies and nurture the next generation of researchers. “Our partnership with KIST, which has been at the forefront of science and technology development in Korea, will further strengthen Sogang’s research and educational capabilities,” Sim said. results.content: Hankuk University of Foreign Studies (HUFS) has signed a memorandum of understanding with the Korea National University of Arts (K-Arts) to expand their joint academic programs. HUFS said the signing ceremony was held Tuesday at HUFS’ Seoul campus, with its President Kang Kee-hoon and K-Arts President Pyeon Jang-wan in attendance. The agreement aims to broaden the scope of the two universities’ joint general education programs, which have been running for 12 years, and strengthen the foundation for interdisciplinary education by leveraging their respective academic resources. results.title: Education minister resigns amid backlash over CSAT anti-cheating measures
results.content: Education Minister Choi Kyo-jin offered to resign Sunday, taking responsibility for confusion over anti-cheating measures in the run-up to the 2027 College Scholastic Ability Test (CSAT). President Lee Jae Myung accepted his resignation within an hour. "Last-minute changes in preparations for the CSAT caused inconvenience to the public, particularly test takers," Choi said in a statement released by the ministry. With the exam now over, Choi acknowledged responsibility for the confusion and announced his decision to step down. The resignation followed mounting criticism of the ministry's slow response to concerns over artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted cheating ahead of the CSAT, Korea's high-stakes college entrance exam. results.title: Sejong University medical device startup secures $9.7 mil. in new investments
results.content: Raywatt, a medical device startup founded by a Sejong University professor, has raised 13 billion won ($9.7 million) in a new funding round, bringing its cumulative funding to more than 23.5 billion won. Ha Jin-yong, a professor in the university’s Department of AI Convergence Electronics Engineering, launched the company in 2019. It specializes in medical imaging devices for cardiovascular and cerebrovascular diagnosis. The investors included participation from InterVest, Life Asset Management, Ryukyung PSG Asset Management, Hyundai Venture Investment, L&S Venture Capital, Eugene Investment & Securities and EcoPro Partners. Investors recognized Raywatt’s achievements in commercializing its technology both in Korea and overseas. results.title: Coast Guard finds vessel-like object on seabed amid search for missing fishing boat
results.content: The Coast Guard said Sunday it has located an object believed to be a sunken vessel on the seabed near where a fishing boat went missing off South Korea's west coast last week. The unidentified object was detected by naval sonar at 7:55 p.m. Saturday, according to the Taean Coast Guard. The object lies 52 meters deep and roughly 41 kilometers northwest of an island off Taean, about 110 km southwest of Seoul. The location is near the site where the fishing boat Haegwangho went missing Wednesday. Officials said they are working to determine whether the object is linked to the vessel. The search entered its fifth day Sunday for the seven crew members who remain missing, as well as the 7.93-ton boat. High waves and strong winds have hampered search and rescue operations. results.title: Hana Financial donates winter supplies, home safety equipment to senior citizens in need
results.content: Hana Financial Group said Sunday that it provided winter supplies and home safety equipment to senior citizens from vulnerable communities as part of efforts to improve their living conditions and prevent household accidents. Hana Financial Chairman Ham Young-joo visited the home of an older woman living alone in Yangcheon-gu, Seoul, Friday, delivering home safety equipment and winter essentials, including blankets, scarves and gloves. “Helping elderly people enjoy a safe and comfortable retirement in the homes they have spent their lives building is a responsibility we all share,” Ham said. “We will continue to bring warmth to their daily lives and work together across the group to build a society where no one is left behind.” The group plans to provide home safety items, including non-slip pads, portable handrails, smoke detectors and household fire extinguishers, to 1,000 seniors who

results.title: Van Gogh Museum bistro drops kimchi sandwich after 'Japanese' labeling controversy
results.content: A restaurant inside the Van Gogh Museum in Amsterdam has changed its menu after it faced criticism for listing a sandwich with kimchi on a menu that cited Japanese but not Korean influences on the cuisine served. Seo Kyung-duk, a professor at Sungshin Women’s University and an advocate for Korean culture, said Sunday that a recent visitor to the Van Gogh Museum found the kimchi sandwich missing from Bistro Vincent’s menu. The item had been replaced with a new item described as including Japanese milk bread. The change comes about six months after the controversy first emerged in May. Sunday was also Kimchi Day in Korea, observed annually on Nov. 22. Bistro Vincent describes its cuisine as French food with a Japanese twist, made with Dutch ingredients. results.title: Korea's car trade deficit with China hits record on Tesla EV imports
results.content: South Korea's deficit in the car trade with China rose to a record high in the January-October period on rising demand for Tesla electric vehicles (EVs) made in China, industry data showed Sunday. South Korea exported $168.77 million worth of cars to China in the first 10 months of the year, down 34.9 percent from the same period last year, according to data from the Korea International Trade Association (KITA) and the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Resources. However, its imports of cars from China surged 79.2 percent on-year to $4.39 billion over the cited period, bringing the trade deficit to a record $4.23 billion. South Korea has recorded a deficit in the car trade with China every year since 2017, with the gap widening sharply from $466 million in 2022 to $943 million in 2023 and $1.73 billion in 2024. results.title: Korea expected to become world's 4th-largest exporter this year
results.content: South Korea is expected to rank fourth globally in annual exports this year after its cumulative exports surpassed $1 trillion for the first time last week, data showed Sunday. According to data from the World Trade Organization (WTO) and U.N. Comtrade, a trade statistics database run by the United Nations, South Korea posted $595.3 billion in exports in the first seven months of 2026. It ranked fifth, behind China with $2.52 trillion, the United States with $1.44 trillion, Germany with $1.12 trillion and the Netherlands with $627.7 billion. The Ministry of Trade, Industry and Resources said it believes South Korea overtook the Netherlands after July as exports accelerated, driven by strong semiconductor shipments amid an artificial intelligence (AI) boom. results.title: Visiting Jeonju Hanok Village
results.content: The hanok village in Jeonju, North Jeolla Province, has been recognized as a “Slow City,” one where life moves at a slower pace. In the first week of October, I visited this village for two day trip. Jeonju Hanok Village, consisting of more than 700 traditional Korean tiled-roof houses, bringing in huge crowds of visitors to enjoy the harmony of the village’s old stone walls and its paths paved with granite flagstones. In the 1910s, when the Japanese colonial government demolished the city walls of Jeonju and began building Japanese-style houses, some citizens left and moved to the present location of the hanok village. In the 1930s, rich residents from the outskirts of Jeonju moved to the area, which took on the appearance of the modern hanok village. results.title: SK chair urges Korea-Japan joint AI talent development program
results.content: SK Group Chairman Chey Tae-won has called for a fundamental overhaul of education to prepare for an artificial intelligence (AI)-native society, urging Korean and Japanese universities and businesses to jointly develop talent for the AI era. Chey made the remarks at Tokyo Forum 2026 on Saturday, emphasizing the need to redesign education systems for a society in which AI is accepted as an integral part of everyday life rather than simply used as a tool. The two-day forum, co-hosted by the Chey Institute for Advanced Studies and the University of Tokyo, started Friday under the theme "AI as a Transformative Technology: Humanity, Knowledge and Civilization." It brought together global experts, including French government AI envoy Anne Bouverot and Sakana AI co-founder Ren Ito. results.title: Seoul district prepares to bring pet funerals directly to residents' doors
results.content: Courier scooters in Seoul deliver everything from midnight kimchi stew to designer handbags in under an hour, and soon grieving pet owners in the city's east will be able to summon a hearse just as easily. Starting in December, Seongdong District, located just east of downtown Seoul, will roll out a municipal mobile pet funeral service, dispatching specialized vans to residents' homes to collect deceased pets, hold a memorial ceremony and perform odorless, smoke-free cremations before returning the ashes in an urn. The initiative, finalized through a partnership signed earlier this month between the district office and local pet funeral operator Petmoon, tackles a thorny urban dilemma in Korea’s densely packed capital. results.title: Herbalife Korea builds next chapter on 30 years of trust
results.content: Herbalife Korea’s next phase of growth will depend on lasting customer relationships rather than individual transactions, Herbalife Korea General Manager Sean Chung said, as the company marks its 30th anniversary in Korea by overhauling distributor compensation and introducing AI tools. The company’s history has been about helping Koreans build healthy nutrition habits, he said, arguing that sustainable growth comes from maintaining trust beyond a single sale. Since entering Korea in 1996, Herbalife has expanded from weight management products into everyday nutrition, protein, sports nutrition and beauty-related wellness as consumer priorities have evolved. Its first decade centered on its flagship Formula 1 shake brand, balancing nutrient intake and healthy eating habits in a market dominated by physical stores and face-to-face sales. results.title: Mountain festival brings foreign tourists to Seoul's peaks
results.content: In a sprawling metropolis better known globally for neon-lit shopping districts, K-pop studios and royal palaces, some of Seoul’s hottest tourist attractions this fall required sturdy boots and a willingness to work up a sweat. More than 13,000 hikers passed through Seoul’s mountain tourism centers during the three weeks of 2026 Seoul Hiking Week, which wrapped up Sunday, underscoring how Korea’s capital is successfully turning its rugged granite peaks into an urban playground. According to the Seoul Tourism Organization, which hosted the third edition of the autumn festival starting on Oct. 26, roughly 4,800 of the visitors to its three Seoul Hiking Tourism Centers were foreign nationals — a 48 percent jump from the same period in 2025. results.title: More Chinese than Korean members: Why K-pop is becoming more multicultural
results.content: Six. That is the number of Chinese members in A2O Soul, the new group recently launched by producer Lee Soo-man's A2O Entertainment as he returns to Korea's K-pop market after a three-year hiatus. The multinational group consists of 15 members, with Chinese nationals accounting for 40 percent, the largest share of any nationality. Korean nationals, including those with dual citizenship, make up five members, or 33.3 percent. It is the first time a K-pop group debuting in Korea has more Chinese members than Korean ones. Multinational groups are nothing new in K-pop. However, among groups debuting in Korea, rather than overseas-localized acts, Korean members have traditionally made up the largest nationality group. results.title: Why are young Koreans falling for Japanese animated series 'Chiikawa?'
results.content: "I'm worried everything will sell out. They'll keep restocking, right?" A long line of customers stretched outside the Chiikawa Shop on the third floor of I'Park Mall in Yongsan District, Seoul, Nov. 5. A quick count put the number of people waiting at well over 50. They had come to buy merchandise featuring characters from the Japanese animated series "Chiikawa." One shopper, surnamed Kim, 27, emerged carrying a large bag filled with stuffed toys, figurines and key rings. "I came to love the animation because I find hope in the way Chiikawa overcomes life's hardships and grows along the way," Kim said with a laugh. "I kept adding things to my basket and ended up spending 460,000 won ($315)."
